title: THE NO-TRACE PLACEHOLDER EXECUTION ID IS DERIVED FROM GOAL TEXT, SO INDEPENDENT RUNS COLLIDE AND BECOME INDISTINGUISHABL
description: THE NO-TRACE PLACEHOLDER EXECUTION ID IS DERIVED FROM GOAL TEXT, SO INDEPENDENT RUNS COLLIDE AND BECOME INDISTINGUISHABLE. MEASURED 2026-09-05. Two separate dispatches of byte-identical goal text — 7f95fc62-aa2a-41a2-9cda-53035b95ecd5 and 5ecc06f1-0eaa-47b1-8950-9dac4d7257ec — each ran independently (distinct dispatchIds, neither carrying a coalesced flag) and each reported the SAME executionId: goal-seek:no-trace:996addc0. When a goal-seek yields no trace the placeholder id appears to be minted from the goal text, so every run of that text collides on one identifier. WHY THIS MATTERS: an executionId is the join key between a dispatch and what it did. When two runs share one, the trace view cannot distinguish them — you cannot tell whether a goal ran once or five times, nor which attempt produced which outcome. It also actively misleads: I inferred from the repeated id that a retry had been coalesced onto an earlier failure, filed that as a defect, and was wrong. The collision is a correctness problem for auditing, and it manufactured a false finding in a session whose whole purpose was auditing. This compounds the already-filed observation that direct resolver invocation is entirely untraced: goals that produce no trace get an id that is not unique, so the thin end of the tracing story is thinner than a count of executions suggests. FALSIFIER: closed only when two independent dispatches of identical goal text that both fail without a trace are shown to carry DISTINCT executionIds — cite both dispatch ids and both execution ids. A closure that only shows a traced goal producing a unique id is fabricated, because the defect is specific to the no-trace placeholder path.
